stem: A company's profit P (in Rs lakh) from selling x thousand units satisfies the condition: (2x - 3) / (x - 5) < 1, where x > 5. For how many integer values of x strictly greater than 5 and at most 12 does this inequality hold?

per_option_rationale.rationale: (2x-3)/(x-5) < 1 => (2x-3)/(x-5) - 1 < 0 => (2x-3-(x-5))/(x-5) < 0 => (x+2)/(x-5) < 0. Since x>5, (x-5)>0 and (x+2)>0 (as x>5>-2), so (x+2)/(x-5)>0 for ALL x>5. The inequality is NEVER satisfied for x>5. Therefore 0 integer values in (5,12].
Cross-multiplying without checking sign of (x-5): 2x-3<x-5 gives x<-2. A sign error makes someone interpret this as x in (5,8) giving 3 values.
Not recognising that (x+2)/(x-5)>0 for x>5, instead incorrectly solving as if the ratio could be negative and counting 5 values in (5,10).
Counting all integers from 6 to 12 inclusive gives 7 values; selecting this assumes the inequality is satisfied for all x>5, missing the analysis.

explanation: Rewrite: (2x-3)/(x-5) < 1. Subtract 1 from both sides: [(2x-3) - (x-5)] / (x-5) < 0 => (x+2)/(x-5) < 0. For this fraction to be negative, numerator and denominator must have opposite signs. Since x>5, (x-5)>0. Also x>5 implies x>-2, so (x+2)>0. Both factors are positive, so (x+2)/(x-5)>0 for all x>5. The inequality (x+2)/(x-5)<0 has NO solution in x>5. Therefore 0 integer values.

explanation_sections.punchline: The hidden trap: after rearranging to (x+2)/(x-5)<0, both factors are positive for all x>5, so the inequality is NEVER satisfied in the given domain.
explanation_sections.approach: Rational inequality: (i) do NOT cross-multiply directly (sign of denominator matters). (ii) Bring 1 to the left: (2x-3)/(x-5)-1<0. (iii) Combine over common denominator: (x+2)/(x-5)<0. (iv) Sign analysis: for x>5, denominator=x-5>0 and numerator=x+2>7>0. Product positive, so expression >0, never <0. Answer: 0 values.
explanation_sections.lesson: Never cross-multiply a rational inequality without first checking the sign of the denominator. Instead, bring everything to one side and do sign analysis on the resulting fraction.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds. The decisive move is recognising that x>5 makes BOTH (x-5) and (x+2) positive, killing the inequality entirely. The trap is cross-multiplying as if (x-5)>0 but forgetting to re-examine the combined numerator. Options 2 and 3 represent partial-credit errors.
